pages.h1: How to make money fast in GTA 6
pages.description: I rob early, sell cars, then use Chapter 3 robberies and Chapter 4 drops. The guides publish ranges, not a single total.
pages.lead: Early on, I rob Illegal Operations and sell the drugs to my fence, and I sell stolen cars at Pay 'n' Spray or to Moses. From Chapter 3 the snap gun opens back-door robberies worth $6,000 to $15,000, and Pilot Pete's drops in Chapter 4 pay $10,000 to $20,000 a run.

sections.h2: What I do in the opening chapters
paragraphs: I stick to the jobs the guides name for the early chapters, and I do not smooth over a name they spell two ways.
These are the ranges and examples in the fact file. I have not turned them into an hourly rate.

sections.h2: Where the sale limit is not settled
paragraphs: I am leaving the Pay 'n' Spray sale limit as a disagreement.

pages.h1: How do you buy a car in GTA 6?
pages.description: I have not found a dealer. I steal a car and pay to register it, and WAiNK shows the fee first.
pages.lead: I have not found a dealer in the guides so far. I steal a car, then pay to register it: with Moses from Chapter 2, at Pay 'n' Spray from Chapter 3, and high-end cars with Randy. The WAiNK app shows each car's registration cost before I take it.

paragraphs: I am careful with the no dealer line, because the fact file says that part is inferred from silence.

sections.h2: Parking is not the same as owning
paragraphs: A garage can keep a stolen car safe. That still does not make it mine.

pages.h1: All GTA 6 garage prices and locations
pages.description: I list 10 garages, from $4,000 to $40,000, plus two free ones. Slot counts differ between the guides.
pages.lead: There are 10 garages, from Mitchel Auto Center at $4,000 to Atlantic Court in Ocean Beach at $40,000, bought in the Vice City Real Estate app. Two are free: Port Gellhorn Station from Moses, and Paradise Garage with the Ultimate Edition.

paragraphs: These are the 10 garages in the fact file, in the stored order, with the dollar prices GameSpot published. I have not converted them to pounds.
Sources differ on capacity, so I show both accounts and I do not invent a slot count for each address.

pages.h1: Can you buy a house in GTA 6?
pages.description: No. I cannot buy a home in GTA 6. The estate app sells garages, and safehouses come with the story.
pages.lead: No. I cannot buy my own home. The Vice City Real Estate app only sells garages, and safehouses come with the story.

paragraphs: Garages are the property in the reputable coverage. The prices are on the garage page.

pages.h1: How to save in GTA 6
pages.description: I open Start or Options, choose Game, and use one of 15 slots. A cheat blocks saving for that session.
pages.lead: I press Start or Options, choose Game, pick one of 15 slots and select Save Game. There is also one autosave slot, but I cannot save during a mission, and using a cheat stops saving for that session.

sections.h2: If I mess up during a mission
paragraphs: This is not a save. It is how I undo a mistake while a mission is still running.

pages.h1: How to switch between Jason and Lucia
pages.description: Switching unlocks after Breakfast Run. I hold Right on the D-pad and pick Jason or Lucia.
pages.lead: Free switching unlocks after the Chapter 2 mission 'Breakfast Run'. After that, I hold Right on the D-pad and pick a character in the bottom right. The same menu can summon my partner or split us up.

pages.h1: How to lose your wanted level (heat) in GTA 6
pages.description: I leave the red heat zone, then clear heat with clothes, a respray, a stowed weapon, or by splitting up.
pages.lead: First I break line of sight and get out of the red heat zone on the map. Then I clear each heat icon: I change my outfit or put on a hat and sunglasses, swap or respray the car, stow longarms, split from my partner, and destroy CCTV.

sections.h2: How many stars a crime is worth
paragraphs: I only have one source for those star counts, and another guide is looser, so I treat the numbers as approximate.

pages.h1: GTA 6 cheats and how to unlock them
pages.description: Cheats unlock after the story. I enter them on the phone, and saving stops for that session.
pages.lead: Cheats only unlock after I finish the story, and each one needs its own challenge. To enter one, I open the phone, hold L1 and R1 (LB and RB) and press the D-pad code. The $250,000 cheat is Up, Right, Down, Left, Up, Left, Down, Right, and it disables saving.

sections.h2: The code I can actually publish
paragraphs: Many codes are still unknown. I am not filling the blanks.

pages.h1: When did GTA 6 come out in the UK?
pages.description: GTA 6 unlocked in the UK at midnight GMT on 19 November 2026. This page records that launch.
pages.lead: It has already happened. GTA 6 unlocked at midnight GMT on Thursday 19 November 2026 on PS5 and Xbox Series X|S. PS5 copies unlocked by store region, and Xbox players could start earlier by changing their time zone. I am writing this on 20 November 2026, so this is a record of the launch.

sections.h2: What had already happened by the next day
paragraphs: Read this as history. The UK unlock was midnight GMT on 19 November 2026, and I checked the record on 20 November 2026.
One of these points is only reported, and the note on US time zones is unclear in the source, so I am not tidying it up.

pages.h1: How much is GTA 6 in the UK? Standard vs Ultimate
pages.description: UK Standard is £69.99 and Ultimate is £89.99. A boxed copy is a download code, not a disc.
pages.lead: Standard costs £69.99 and Ultimate costs £89.99 (US $79.99 and $99.99). Ultimate is digital and adds the '95 Grotti Cheetah, extra revolvers, a garage and a buggy, and five extra shops. Boxed copies contain a download code, not a disc.

paragraphs: I do not have a confirmed UK price for a standalone Ultimate upgrade. The fact file says that part is still unknown.
The contents below are the list stored in the fact file. I have not shortened the names.

pages.h1: How big is GTA 6? File size and storage
pages.description: I would clear 212GB. Rockstar says up to 212GB, and PlayStation says at least 212GB.
pages.lead: Rockstar says up to 212GB depending on the device, and the PlayStation page says to clear at least 212GB. Preload opened on 10 November. I would clear 212GB, because the fact file says that is the safe reading when the wording differs.

paragraphs: The wording differs, so I am not pretending the two pages say the same thing.

pages.h1: Does GTA 6 have online multiplayer?
pages.description: Not at launch. It is a single player game so far, and no online mode or date has been announced.
pages.lead: Not at launch. Rockstar calls GTA 6 a single-player experience and has not announced an online mode or a date, though existing GTA Online carries on.

paragraphs: I am labelling this as speculation so it does not read like a date.

pages.h1: Is GTA 6 on PC?
pages.description: Not yet. GTA 6 is on PS5 and Xbox Series X|S. A reported PC date is still unconfirmed.
pages.lead: Not yet. It is on PS5 and Xbox Series X|S only, and Xbox One can play through Xbox Cloud Gaming. A GamesBeat report says a PC release in Q1 2027, but Rockstar has not confirmed it.

sections.h2: Where I can play it now

paragraphs: This report is unconfirmed. I am not treating Q1 2027 as a release date.

pages.h1: How does the bank (BuckMe) and Family Savings work?
pages.description: I can hold $20,000 in cash and I lose it if I am Wasted or Busted. Family Savings cannot be withdrawn.
pages.lead: Each character can carry up to $20,000 in cash, and I lose it if I am Wasted or Busted, so I bank it at an ATM. Purchases over $1,000 go through BuckMe checking. Money in Family Savings can never come back out, and it affects the ending.

paragraphs: The guides say the balance limits rise later in the story. They do not state the dollar amount of each limit, so I am not filling those in.
The guides name five tiers. They do not list a dollar amount for each tier in the fact I have.

pages.h1: Where to find a tank in GTA 6
pages.description: The Hauners Rhino tanks in the guide are at Mile Zero Air Station. Getting spotted means five stars.
pages.lead: The only Hauners Rhino tanks found so far are at Mile Zero Air Station, west of Key Lento in the Leonida Keys, usually in the hangars. If I am spotted getting in, I get an instant five-star wanted level.

sections.h2: The only place the guide names

paragraphs: The five-star warning sits on the normal star scale, which goes up to six.

pages.h1: How to steal cars in GTA 6 (slim jim, key cloner, trackers)
pages.description: I scan with WAiNK, use a slim jim from Chapter 2, and a key cloner from Chapter 3 for keyless cars.
pages.lead: I scan a car with the WAiNK app first. A slim jim from Moses in Chapter 2 opens locks quietly, and the key cloner from Chapter 3 is needed for keyless cars. Advanced trackers alert the police unless I keep driving fast.

sections.h2: Selling, and the limit the guides do not share

pages.h1: Every GTA 6 phone app and what it does
pages.description: I press Up for the phone. BuckMe, RydeMe, Scooter Bros, WAiNK and Vice City Real Estate are the key apps.
pages.lead: I press Up on the D-pad for the phone. The key apps are BuckMe for the bank, RydeMe for a taxi and fast travel, Scooter Bros for car delivery, WAiNK for the car scanner, and Vice City Real Estate for garages.

paragraphs: I have not added any app that is missing from this list.

pages.h1: How long is GTA 6 and how many missions?
pages.description: There are 91 main missions. The story is 65+ hours, side content is 90 to 100, and 100% is past 200.
pages.lead: There are 91 main missions over five chapters. GameSpot puts the story at 65+ hours, 90 to 100 hours with side content, and 200+ hours for 100%.

paragraphs: The opening is long, and free character switching is one of the things that waits.

pages.h1: What do my chosen GTA 6 garages cost?
pages.description: I add the published garage prices and show both slot readings, because the guides do not agree.
pages.lead: I add up the garage prices from the list of 10, then I show slot capacity both ways. PC Gamer counts one car per garage. GameSpot says one or a couple, and gives Valentina's garage two slots.

paragraphs: Shore Court is in the note below. I do not have a price or a slot count for it, so it is not a tick.

pages.h1: What payout ranges do the GTA 6 guides publish?
pages.description: I show activity payout ranges and the cash limits. These are estimates from published guides, not exact sums.
pages.lead: I can line the published payout ranges up next to the cash limits. I show ranges only, and I never add them into an exact sum. These are estimates from published guides.

paragraphs: Every line below is the wording stored in the fact file. These figures are estimates from published guides.

pages.h1: Which GTA 6 cheat codes have been published?
pages.description: I can search the one money code in the fact file. Many GTA 6 cheat codes are still unknown.
pages.lead: I can search the cheat list that is actually in the fact file. There is one published code, for $250,000, and it unlocks when I finish the story. Many codes are still unknown.

pages.h1: What is this GTA 6 fan guide?
pages.description: An unofficial fan guide. I copy each game fact from published outlets and I keep the link.
pages.lead: I wrote this as an unofficial fan guide for people starting GTA 6. I am not affiliated with Rockstar Games or Take-Two.
pages.sources_note: This page explains the method. It does not add a game fact. The links are example articles already stored in the fact file, one for each outlet name, so you can see the kind of source I use.

sections.h2: How a fact gets onto a page
paragraphs: Every game fact on the question pages is copied from the fact file in this project. I keep the outlet and the link with the claim.
The fact file limits me to these outlets: {{scope_note}}
Where the file says the sources differ, or that something is unknown, reported, or speculation, I say that in plain words. I do not pick a winner, and I do not fill a gap from a fan wiki.
I do not use official artwork, official typefaces, or official marks. The shapes at the top of the page are mine. There are no ads and no trackers.
The date on each page is the day I last checked the fact file: {{checked}}.

pages.h1: What data does this fan guide collect?
pages.description: None. This static guide has no accounts, no analytics, and no third party scripts.
pages.lead: I do not collect accounts, messages, or analytics. The pages are static files.
pages.sources_note: This page does not state a game fact, so there is no outlet list.

paragraphs: I do not embed third party scripts, fonts, or adverts. Loading a page does not call an analytics service.
If a host such as GitHub serves these files, that host can keep its own connection logs. I do not receive those logs, and I cannot see who you are.
The planners do not write to storage on your machine. When you leave the page, the ticks are gone.
I do not sell or share personal data, because this guide does not take any.

pages.h1: Does this fan guide use cookies?
pages.description: No. I do not set cookies, and the planners forget your ticks when you leave the page.
pages.lead: No. I do not set cookies, and I do not store your planner ticks.
pages.sources_note: This page does not state a game fact, so there is no outlet list.

paragraphs: I do not set cookies. I do not use local storage, session storage, or anything similar to remember you.
There is no consent banner, because there is nothing to accept.
If you followed a link from somewhere else, that other site may use its own cookies. Once you are here, I do not add any.
